page: The Vultr vbm-24c-384gb-amd is a dedicated bare-metal server in the Bare Metal SSD family, structured for memory-intensive and multi-threaded enterprise workloads. It is powered by a 24-core, 48-thread AMD EPYC 9254 processor built on the x86_64 architecture with a base clock frequency of 2.9 GHz. CPU cache allocation includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. The system is provisioned with 384 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 6 GHz, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage is provided via a bundled 960 GB local SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server operates without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results validate strong compute and memory subsystem capabilities. The AMD EPYC 9254 achieves top-tier results in single-core and multi-core evaluations, scoring 2272.0 on single-core and 21196.0 on multi-core in Geekbench testing. Stress-ng multi-core testing records 83358.94 points, while single-core reaches 3473.59 points. PassMark benchmarks reflect strong compute output at 71773.64 points alongside high memory subsystem efficiency at 3310.61 points. Memory throughput reaches 296.64 GB/sec on large uncached read operations and 164.02 GB/sec on uncached writes. The CPU instruction set includes AVX-512 extensions such as VNNI and BF16, facilitating 4386.48 tokens/sec prompt processing and 390.91 tokens/sec text generation on small LLM architectures.

The bare-metal architecture removes hypervisor overhead, delivering predictable latency and full hardware utilization. While local storage is limited to a single 960 GB SSD, the high memory-to-core allocation provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound tasks relative to standard virtualization instances. These attributes make the server well matched for high-throughput in-memory datastores such as Redis (demonstrated at 72.25 million operations per second), relational database management systems, large software build farms, and memory-constrained data transformation pipelines.
description: Vultr vbm-24c-384gb-amd is a dedicated bare-metal server configured for memory-intensive and throughput-sensitive workloads. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9254 processor with 24 physical cores running at 2.9 GHz across 48 vCPUs, the hardware delivers top-tier CPU performance alongside 384 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 system memory. Bundled local storage includes a 960 GB SSD, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address, with no discrete GPU accelerators present. Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-core and multi-core capabilities, achieving top-decile Geekbench and stress-ng rankings. High memory bandwidth, exceeding 296 GB/sec on uncached reads, pairs with strong Redis processing throughput of over 72 million operations per second and robust AVX-512 instruction support for quantized CPU inference tasks. With an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, the system offers substantial resource density without virtualization overhead, making it well matched for in-memory caching layers, large relational database engines, compilation clusters, and mid-scale analytics pipelines.
